# Synthetic cross-method research excerpts

These are isolated invented exercises, not real papers or people. Each case is
self-contained. No web sources, images, ethics records or original files beyond
this text are supplied. Missing materials are not claims that such materials
exist. Evaluate each case using the methods it actually employs.

## FORMAL: an argument about real numbers

F1. Proposition: For every real number x, x squared is strictly greater than x.
F2. Proof: Write x squared minus x as x(x - 1). Both factors are positive, so the
product is positive. Therefore the proposition holds for every real number.
F3. This is a formal argument with no experiment, participants or numerical study.

## QUALITATIVE: interpretive interviews

Q1. Twelve volunteers discussed daily travel. The paper uses a reflexive thematic
approach and does not claim population representativeness or statistical tests.
Q2. Public transcripts are restricted to protect participants. De-identified
excerpts are supplied for interpretation; no transcript upload is authorized.
Q3. The Results says: "No participant described using a bus for a daily commute."
Q4. Participant excerpt P3 says: "I take the bus to work each weekday morning."
Q5. The paper does not report p-values, inter-rater agreement or a numerical
saturation threshold. No legal or ethics-policy determination is requested.

## ARCHIVAL: edition-specific source interpretation

H1. A supplied transcription is labeled: Archive of the Fictional Borough,
collection B, volume 7, folio 12r, source date 1902; original script: "ألف".
H2. Transcription: "The bridge opened this spring, 1902."
H3. The article's paragraph 4 claims: "Folio 12r explicitly dates the bridge's
opening to spring 1912."
H4. The archive has no public URL or DOI. No original scan, catalogue access or
independent authenticity check is supplied. A later catalogue date is not given.

## COMPUTATIONAL: a classifier benchmark

C1. The paper divides records into a training set and a held-out test set.
C2. It states that features are standardized using the mean and standard deviation
computed from all records before splitting, including the held-out test records.
C3. Hyperparameters are selected by maximizing the same test-set score that is
reported as the final held-out evaluation. No independent final set is described.
C4. Code, predictions, seeds and data are not supplied, so execution and numerical
reproduction are not possible from this excerpt.

## ENGINEERING: energy units

E1. The paper reports constant electrical power of 10 watts for 2 seconds.
E2. Its Results states: "The delivered energy is 20 joules, equivalent to 20
watt-hours." It uses the ordinary definitions of watt, joule and hour.
E3. No instrument, hardware test, raw measurement or calibration record is supplied.

## SYNTHESIS: overlapping primary evidence

S1. A narrative review discusses reports A and B, explicitly describing both as
analyses of the same 40-person cohort and the same follow-up period.
S2. Its conclusion claims the two reports supply "80 independent participants"
supporting the association. No additional cohort is described.
S3. It is a narrative review, not a pooled-effect meta-analysis. No conclusion
about heterogeneity statistics, clinical registration or a specific reporting
checklist is requested.
